instructions:
FF Montage is a desktop video editor; these tools edit the project open in its window (the user sees every change and can undo with Ctrl+Z).
Model: one main video track (clips in time order, gaps allowed, transitions only between adjacent clips) plus audio tracks for music/voice. All times are seconds.
Workflow: get_project → import_media (absolute paths) → add_clip (track "video"/"audio") → trim/move with update_clip, split_clip, delete_clip (ripple), close_gaps → set_transition (clip_id = second clip of the cut) → get_frame / detect_silence to inspect → save_project → export_video, then export_status with wait.
Ids come from get_project; re-read it after edits because splitting creates new clip ids.
Do not use force=true in new_project/open_project without asking the user.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: Return the whole project state: media library (ids, paths, durations, resolution, fps), the main video track (clips with timeline start/end and source in/out, volume, fades, transitions, reversed/freeze flags), audio tracks, gaps, playhead, undo/redo availability and export status. All times are in seconds. Call this first and after edits.

tools.name: import_media
tools.title: Import media files
tools.description: Add video/audio files from disk to the project media library (does not put them on the timeline). Paths must be absolute. Returns media ids with duration (seconds), resolution, fps and whether the file has video/audio. Importing the same file twice returns the existing id.

tools.name: add_clip
tools.title: Add clip to timeline
tools.description: Place a media file (or a part of it) on the timeline. track "video" = the single main video track (the clip also carries the file's own sound); track "audio" = an audio track (music, voice-over). Video without start is appended to the end of the video track. If start is given and the place is occupied, the clip snaps to a nearby gap or is inserted before/after the clip it hits (later clips move right); with insert=true it is placed exactly at start and later clips are pushed right. Audio without start goes to 0 s; if the chosen track is busy, a free or new track is used. source_in/source_out select the fragment of the file (seconds, default whole file).

start.description: Timeline position of the clip start, seconds

source_in.description: Fragment start inside the file, seconds (default 0)

source_out.description: Fragment end inside the file, seconds (default = file duration)

audio_track_id.description: For track "audio": audio track id from get_project, or "new" for a new track

insert.description: Video only: place exactly at start and push later clips right (default false)

tools.name: update_clip
tools.title: Update clip
tools.description: Change a clip: trim (source_in/source_out or duration, seconds), move (start, seconds; video clips push the following clips right if needed, unless the place is free), volume (0..2, 1 = original), muted, fades (fade_in/fade_out, seconds), name, or move an audio clip to another audio track (audio_track_id or "new"). Trimming leaves a gap — use close_gaps to remove it. For reversed clips source_in/source_out are in the ORIGINAL file time and must stay within the reversed fragment.

source_in.description: New fragment start inside the file, seconds

source_out.description: New fragment end inside the file, seconds

duration.description: New clip length, seconds (changes source_out; useful for freeze frames)

audio_track_id.description: Audio clips only: move to this audio track id, or "new"

insert.description: Video only, with start: place exactly at start and push later clips right

tools.name: split_clip
tools.title: Split clip
tools.description: Cut a clip into two at a timeline time (seconds). Without clip_id the video clip under that time is split; pass clip_id to split an audio clip. The cut must be at least 0.1 s from the clip edges. Returns both halves.

time.description: Timeline time of the cut, seconds

tools.name: delete_clip
tools.title: Delete clip
tools.description: Remove a clip from the timeline (the file stays in the media library). ripple=true shifts the following clips of the same track left by the clip length, so no gap remains.

tools.name: reverse_clip
tools.title: Reverse clip
tools.description: Toggle reverse playback of a video clip fragment (plays backwards). FFmpeg renders the reversed fragment, which may take a while for long clips. Calling again restores normal direction.

tools.name: freeze_frame
tools.title: Freeze frame
tools.description: Insert a still frame of the video at a timeline time: the clip is split there, a freeze-frame clip of the given duration is inserted and everything to the right moves right by that duration.

tools.name: set_transition
tools.title: Set transition
tools.description: Set the transition between two adjacent video clips. clip_id is the SECOND clip of the junction (the one the transition leads into); it must start exactly where the previous clip ends (no gap — use close_gaps first). type: one of fade, fadeblack, fadewhite, wipeleft, wiperight, wipeup, wipedown, smoothleft, smoothright, smoothup, smoothdown, slideleft, slideright, slideup, slidedown, circleopen, circleclose, zoomin, hblur, blinds, or "none" to remove. duration in seconds (0.1..3, default 0.5; limited by clip lengths). The transition is centred on the cut and does not change the total length.

clip_id.description: Id of the second clip of the junction

tools.name: close_gaps
tools.title: Close gaps
tools.description: Remove empty space on a track by shifting clips left. track: "video" or an audio track id. With time (seconds) only the gap containing that time is closed; otherwise all gaps on the track (including the one at the start). Other tracks are not moved.

time.description: A time inside the gap to close, seconds

tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo
tools.description: Undo the last edit (same as Ctrl+Z in the app).

tools.name: redo
tools.title: Redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone edit (same as Ctrl+Y).

tools.name: set_playhead
tools.title: Set playhead
tools.description: Move the playhead (preview position) to a timeline time in seconds, so the user sees that moment.

tools.name: new_project
tools.title: New project
tools.description: Start a new empty project. Fails if the current project has unsaved changes unless force=true (ask the user before forcing; or save_project first).

tools.name: open_project
tools.title: Open project
tools.description: Open a saved .ffproj project file (absolute path). Fails if the current project has unsaved changes unless force=true.

tools.name: save_project
tools.title: Save project
tools.description: Save the project as a .ffproj file. Without path: saves to the current file, or to the projects folder with the project name if it was never saved. Returns the path.

path.description: Absolute path (.ffproj is appended if missing)

tools.name: export_video
tools.title: Export video
tools.description: Render the timeline to an MP4 file in the background and return immediately; poll export_status. codec: av1 (smallest, default), hevc, h264 (most compatible); NVIDIA GPU is used when available. quality: high (default), medium, compact. resolution: source (default) or 2160/1440/1080/720 (height, keeps aspect). fps: frames per second (default: as source). Without path the file goes to the output folder named after the project.

path.description: Absolute output path (.mp4 is appended if missing); existing file is replaced

tools.name: export_status
tools.title: Export status
tools.description: State of the current/last export: idle, running (fraction 0..1, eta seconds), done (output path, size), error or cancelled. wait (seconds, up to 120) blocks until the export finishes or the time passes, to avoid frequent polling.

wait.description: Wait up to N seconds for completion (0..120)

tools.name: cancel_export
tools.title: Cancel export
tools.description: Stop the running export (the partial file is deleted).

tools.name: get_frame
tools.title: Get frame
tools.description: Look at the video: returns a JPEG image of one frame. Either time (timeline seconds; shows the source frame of the video clip there, without fades/transitions; in a gap the result is a black frame) or media_id + source_time (seconds inside the file). width: image width in pixels (default 640, max 1920).

source_time.description: Time inside the media file, seconds (with media_id)

tools.name: detect_silence
tools.title: Detect silence
tools.description: Find quiet parts of the sound (pauses in speech, silence) with FFmpeg silencedetect. Give media_id (times in the file) or clip_id (only inside the clip fragment; also returns timeline times). threshold_db: loudness below which is silence (default -35 dB; -50 stricter, -25 looser). min_duration: shortest pause to report, seconds (default 0.5).
